issues.title: Lower cardinality estimate for substring-match table filters
issues.hypothesis: Every non-equality table filter is costed with a flat DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY=0.2 (relation_statistics_helper.cpp:146-151; same constant in relation_manager.cpp:199/258/276/293/374 for filters left in a LogicalFilter). A predicate that requires a literal substring (contains(col,'lit'), col LIKE '%lit%', LIKE '%a%b%') is usually far more selective than a range comparison. Evidence from q09: p_name LIKE '%ghost%' is actually about 5% selective. EXPLAIN estimates 1,256,266 rows for lineitem⋈part⋈orders and 5,057,324 for the top join, but EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows 324,507 rows, a 4-15x overestimate. Because of that the optimizer builds hash tables on orders (1.5M rows) and on partsupp⋈supplier⋈nation (800k rows), and each of those two joins costs about 0.22-0.23s CPU, while the real probe side is only 324k rows. With a better estimate the join order and build sides can put the small filtered side on the build side.
issues.plan: In RelationStatisticsHelper::ExtractGetStats (src/optimizer/join_order/relation_statistics_helper.cpp, around lines 119-155), when no equality filter fired, check whether any non-optional table filter is an ExpressionFilter whose expression is a positive substring-containment test: a BoundFunctionExpression named 'contains', or '~~' / 'like_escape' whose constant pattern starts with '%' and contains at least one non-wildcard character, possibly nested under CONJUNCTION_AND. Do not match negations (!~~, NOT). If one is found, use base_cardinality * SUBSTRING_MATCH_SELECTIVITY, defined as DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY*DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY (0.04) in relation_statistics_helper.hpp, instead of 0.2. Apply the same classification in relation_manager.cpp where a LogicalFilter's expressions fall back to DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY: add a small static helper IsSubstringMatchPredicate(const Expression&) to RelationStatisticsHelper and reuse it in both places. Before and after the change, check with EXPLAIN on q09/q16 that the estimates move and that the join order changes. Run the full visible bench, since plans may change elsewhere.
issues.expected_gain: q09 (18% of total): possibly 20-40% if the orders/partsupp builds shrink or the join order changes. Smaller effects possible on q16 (s_comment LIKE '%..%..%' under NOT IN) and on other templates with LIKE '%x%' on a dimension table. Roughly 3-8% on the visible geomean if q09 moves.
issues.generality: Any star or snowflake join where a dimension is filtered by a substring/contains predicate (text search on names or comments) now gets a realistic, smaller cardinality, so it is placed on the build side and joined early. Possible regressions: substring predicates that are actually unselective (for example '%a%') will be underestimated, which could put a big relation on the build side. That risk is bounded because the build-side flip and the hash join still work correctly, only slower.
issues.risk: Medium. The change only affects cost estimates, so results stay correct, but plans for other templates may change, possibly for the worse. The selectivity constant is a heuristic derived from DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY, not tuned to the data. If the bench shows a mixed result, try applying it only when the literal has at least 3 characters before giving up.

issues.title: Investigate high-cardinality hash aggregation cost after outer join
issues.hypothesis: In q13, HASH_GROUP_BY on a single integer key (c_custkey) over 1.53M rows into 150k groups costs 0.20s CPU, about 130ns/row and the largest operator in the 2nd slowest template. The group key comes from the build side of a RIGHT join and has tight min/max stats [1,150000]. Each of the 8 threads sees nearly every group (reduction only about 1.3x per thread), so the thread-local tables give little benefit before repartitioning. DecideAdaptation in radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:424 skips lookups only when the HLL unique share is above 0.95.
issues.plan: First profile only (perf on q13), to see whether the cost is in the local sink, the repartition, or the finalize/combine. Candidate fixes, to be chosen after profiling: (a) when the estimated group count from stats is close to the row count per thread, start in skip-lookup/partition-only mode earlier; (b) a dense-range direct aggregation path for a single integer key with a small stats range and simple aggregates. Do not change the perfect_ht_threshold default, which is a setting.
issues.expected_gain: q13 maybe 20-30%. Any template with a GROUP BY on a high-cardinality key (q18 subquery GROUP BY l_orderkey) may also benefit.
issues.generality: GROUP BY on a high-cardinality key with low per-thread reduction, a common pattern in analytical queries (per-customer or per-order aggregates).
issues.risk: Medium-high. The aggregate hash table is heavily tuned, so a constant tweak can regress low-cardinality aggregates. It needs a profile before any coding.

dispatch: Lower cardinality estimate for substring-match table filters
output.memory:
## db_evolve planner memory (duckdb)

### Round log
- G1R1: baseline 1.000x, geomean 40.0ms. Dispatched "Lower cardinality estimate for substring-match table filters" (q09 join estimates 4-15x too high). Backlog: q13 high-cardinality hash agg investigation.

### Tooling facts
- `dbe-tool sql "EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) ..."` hung until the 120s timeout. Plain EXPLAIN piped into `grep -oE "HASH_JOIN|[0-9,]+ rows|[a-z_]+ = [a-z_]+"` works and is cheap for estimates.
- Bash: compound commands (;, multiple pipes) and redirects to /tmp need approval. Use single commands or a single pipe; use the Grep/Read tools for files.
- profile.md truncates big plans (the q09 lower half and the q18 subquery aggregate are missing). Operator times are summed CPU across threads, not wall time.

### Codebase facts (verified)
- LIKE: src/function/scalar/string/like.cpp already has a LikeMatcher (constant pattern split into segments, FindStrInStr via memchr+word compare in contains.cpp). '%x%' is rewritten to contains. LIKE micro-optimization looks low value.
- FSST string scan (src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp StringScanPartial/Select) decompresses every row. The o_comment and similar comment columns are FSST. enable_fsst_vectors defaults to false. Filtering on compressed strings would be a big project.
- Join-order cardinality: RelationStatisticsHelper::DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY=0.2 (relation_statistics_helper.hpp:57). It is applied flat to any non-equality table filter (relation_statistics_helper.cpp:146-151) and in relation_manager.cpp:199,258,276,293,374. InspectTableFilter (line 446) handles only CONJUNCTION_AND and CONSTANT_COMPARISON equality.
- Perfect hash agg: CanUsePerfectHashAggregate in src/execution/physical_plan/plan_aggregate.cpp:127, gated by the perfect_ht_threshold setting (don't change defaults).
- Radix HT adaptation: DecideAdaptation in radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:424 (SKIP_LOOKUP threshold 0.95), MaybeRepartition at :479.

### Profile hotspots (baseline)
- q09 120ms: two hash joins about 0.22s CPU each, building on orders 1.5M and partsupp 800k while the real probe side is 324k. The estimate is wrong because of LIKE '%..%' at 0.2 selectivity (actual about 5%).
- q13 96ms: orders scan with NOT LIKE '%a%b%' 0.22s (FSST decompression + match), RIGHT join 0.11s, HASH_GROUP_BY 150k groups 0.20s.
- q18 82ms: the plan in the profile is truncated. It is likely the GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING subquery over lineitem (1.5M groups). Profile it next.

### Directions
- Promising: cardinality estimates (cheap, plan-level, correctness-safe). Watch for regressions on other templates.
- Unexplored: q18 large aggregation, q13 aggregation, hash join build cost in general.
- Exhausted: none yet.
